title: What is Redux Middleware?
overview: Middleware is a layer between dispatching an action and reaching the reducer. It is used for handling additional logic like API calls, logging, and authentication.

example.title: Middleware Flow
example.content:
Component
 ↓
Dispatch Action
 ↓
Middleware
 ↓
Reducer
 ↓
Store

title: Why Use Middleware?
overview: Middleware allows Redux to handle operations that cannot be performed directly inside reducers, such as asynchronous tasks.

example.title: Middleware Uses
example.content:
✔ API requests
✔ Logging actions
✔ Error handling
✔ Authentication checks

title: Redux Thunk Middleware
overview: Redux Thunk allows action creators to return functions and handle asynchronous operations before dispatching normal actions.

example.title: Thunk Middleware
example.content:
dispatch(fetchUsers())

Middleware handles API call

Then dispatches result action

title: Custom Middleware
overview: Developers can create custom middleware to add application-specific logic during the Redux data flow.

example.title: Custom Middleware Example

overview: You learned how Redux middleware works, why it is needed, and how it helps handle async operations and additional logic.
